Amazing camera work, and a well thought out concept from Jackson Treadway I felt moved by this short film. in the span of 2 minutes, i felt the obsession and frustration of the protagonist, and through a creative choice of lens and filters, i was transported to a raw, gritty perspective on obsession and drive to succeed Amazing job, looking forward to more short films 👍 Jackson Treadway

Obsession es un ejercicio sobre la fijación emocional y el deterioro mental. Tiene una puesta en escena sobria, que deja que la incomodidad crezca sin necesidad de exagerar nada. Lo que más funciona es cómo construye tensión desde lo cotidiano. Puede que no sea un corto que busque impresionar visualmente, pero sí deja un mensaje claro de cómo aquello que nos consume puede dañar a quienes nos rodean. Como primer intento, se siente valioso porque ya muestra intención y una búsqueda de identidad. Gracias al director por presentarme este proyecto.

The only cure for obsession is violence Jackson Treadway, the creator of the short film, introduced me to his project. This film combines good cinematography with great soundtrack. I truly enjoy watching young artists’ projects. Please watch to support this young artist and his project.

Obsession | A Wildly Inventive Horror Spin on Love, Possession, and Personal Space Curry Barker’s Obsession takes a familiar romcom fantasy an awkward guy wishing his crush would love him back, and twists it into something deeply unsettling, darkly funny, and surprisingly sharp. Built on clever writing rather than scale, the film reimagines obsessive affection through grounded horror, where every scene, detail, and escalation serves a purpose. The storytelling constantly flips ordinary gestures of love into disturbing scenarios, creating tension without relying on conventional horror tricks. Michael Johnston convincingly captures the insecurity and panic of the protagonist, while Inde Navarrette is phenomenal in a role that shifts from warmth to terrifying emotional volatility. With inventive visual storytelling, precise atmosphere-building, and a script that finds horror in the collapse of emotional boundaries, Obsession feels refreshingly original. Bottom Line: A creative and confident approach that has been successfully delivered as a smart, unsettling and darkly hilarious horror flick.

Some people love Rollercoasters, or jumping out of planes for a rush or adrenaline; I watch horror films because I hate heights. The last three horror films I watched were Caveat, Oddity and Together; all three made me feel uncomfortable and creeped out. Together more than anything, I started watching it cuddling with my boyfriend, but by the end of the film, I didn't want him anywhere near me for at least 48 hours. But horror films lately have been missing something, something that I longed for. None of them scared me; all of them had a predictable plot, predictable characters, and predictable scares. Until my friend and I saw Obsession at the cinema on Wednesday. I could tell no one in the viewing was going to take it seriously, but we had hope from it being the first 18+ rated horror in a while. It was terrifying. The plot was amazing, and the acting was award-worthy, especially Inde Navarrette; she was absolutely brilliant, and I hope this projects her into more roles. I would love to see her in more horror films for sure. The scares and psychological turmoil were insaneee (in a good way), and you could never predict what was coming next. Even if you've seen clips or audio online and assume you know what it's about, you really don't. They all take you by surprise. I do believe it is more psychological for women to watch, so I suggest if you're a woman, go with your bestie/girlfriend, but if you have a good man, go with him, and he should understand why it's so insane. My friend and I are enthusiastic horror fans, and Obsession was so refreshing because it scared us to the point we left the cinema with our hearts racing and hands shaking.
